newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia PGM exports fail to allay Japan worries.
newsitem.headline: Russia PGM exports fail to allay Japan worries.

text.p: The long-awaited resumption of exports of Russian platinum group metals (PGMs) failed to dispel concerns over the stability of Russian supplies among Japanese end-users who remain determined to cut usage of the metal.
"The protracted suspension of Russian exports taught end-users how risky it is to depend on Russia's palladium," said a senior official of a major bullion house.
"All end-users are seriously considering every possible way not to depend on Russian palladium," he said.

Russia's first PGM shipments to Japan in six months arrived on Thursday. Japanese customers have signed term contracts with Russian platinum group metals export agency (Almazjuvelireport) for July to December PGM deliveries.
Russian exports of PGMs had been suspended since the beginning of this year due to bureaucratic disputes and other domestic problems in Russia.
The suspension by Russia, which supplies more than 60 percent of the world's palladium and about 20 percent of its platinum, sent palladium prices surging to 17-year highs earlier this year.

High prices and the unstable Russian supplies sped up efforts by electronic component makers, which consume about 60 percent of Japan's total palladium demand, to shift to cheaper metals such as nickel.

The quest for a substitute however, is a tougher task for auto catalyst makers, which have yet to find an appropriate substitute and are looking at other ways to avoid using the metal, precious metal industry sources said.
Traders lamented the fact that there were few countries they could rely on for PGM supplies.
"The capacity of countries other than Russia to supply palladium, such as South Africa is limited. We face a dilemma," a trading house trader said.
Japanese traders said they expect PGM prices to ease in the near-term, but the aftereffects of Russia's suspension to continue for some time.
They said there was a widespread view within the industry that Russian PGM exports would be suspended again next year.
"We believe contracted supplies will arrive this year. But the outlook is uncertain for next year," one trader said.

An official at another bullion house said tightness in the domestic market was expected to continue for two or three months, as the supplies would be handed over to customers and would not be used to replenish inventories.
"In the near-term, palladium prices are expected to edge lower to around $140 to $150 per ounce," he said. "The key is maybe whether U.S. based hedge funds will liquidate their longs," he said.
In late Asia on Thursday spot palladium was quoted at around $166.00/170.00 per ounce.
